chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Al-Reza (peace be upon him) who said:
A virgin (wife) who is divorced three times and marains in a non-consummated marriage, has become permanently divorced (ba'in), and is not permissible for her husband until she marries another man.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These narrations indicate what we said, that whoever divorces his wife three times for the sake of the Sunnah, she is not permissible for him until she marries another man, because the 'divorce of the waiting period' does not occur in the case of a virgin or one not yet consummated, and we have clarified that among the conditions of the 'divorce of the waiting period' is cohabitation after the return, and both of these do not occur in the one who has not been entered into.

key_terms.طَلَاقُ الْعِدَّةِ: Divorce of the waiting period (a specific type of revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a virgin wife who receives three divorces before consummation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi cites Imam al-Rida to establish that a triple divorce issued to a virgin before consummation results in a permanent separation (ba'in), distinct from the revocable divorce (raj'i) applicable after consummation. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani reinforces this by noting that the prerequisite of 'consumption' for the validity of the waiting period (iddah) divorce is absent, thereby necessitating a new marriage and consummation (nuzul) for the wife to become lawful again to her first husband.
